description: Mid thesis whose conclusions contradict its own results: 39% name salary first, the conclusions say 70% value non-financial factors most. A 23-person sample from one shop generalised to all small firms; a chapter on Taylor unconnected to the problem; hypotheses never verified.

metadata.author: Julia Wróbel
metadata.title: Motywowanie pracowników z pokolenia Z w małych przedsiębiorstwach

expected.issue: The conclusions contradict the results: the results show salary as the most frequent first choice (39%, 19 top-three mentions), but the conclusions claim about 70% value non-financial factors most.
A sample of 23 employees from a single company (where the author did an internship) is generalised to generation Z in Poland and to all small firms.
The conclusions never state whether H1 and H2 were confirmed or rejected — and the data actually contradict both (salary ranks first; remote work ranks eighth).
Chapter 2 on Taylor's biography and scientific management is not connected to the research problem about generation Z and is not used later in the thesis.

must_not_flag: The introduction has no hypotheses or no research question.
The bibliography has fewer than 25 sources.
There are fewer than four foreign-language sources.
The thesis has no conclusions chapter.
